title: Adaptive cost rendezvous: prefill heuristics and quant consensus
author: Marina Ortega
release_notes: Introduce rendezvous-based prefill allocator and quant-profile consensus algorithm to reduce per-token unit cost under bursty tenant loads; adds a cost-debug CLI flag and unit-econ telemetry points.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed recurring microburst patterns from a subset of tenants where naive prefill and cache policies either over-allocated GPU memory or fell back to expensive low-batch inference. This PR introduces a rendezvous-prefill allocator that coordinates tenant warm-start tokens across concurrent requests, plus a quant-consensus module that reconciles candidate quantization profiles for model variants to avoid oscillation between profiles during rollouts. The goal is to lower token unit-cost and reduce cold-start tail latency without sacrificing quality.

What this PR changes (summary):
- serving/rendezvous_allocator: new component that groups warmup-prefill requests by similarity window and allocates prefill capacity with soft priorities.
- serving/quant_consensus: algorithm and operator that takes profile opinions (loss estimate, perf delta, cost delta) from trial runs and outputs a stable profile using a median-of-opinions + safety floor.
- telemetry/unit_econ: added counters/gauges for prefill hit-rate, rendezvous-group size, quant-profile switches, estimated unit-cost delta.
- cli/cost-debug: new flag --rendezvous-dryrun to simulate decisions and produce a compact CSV for offline accounting.
- e2e integration tests and a small perf harness for synthetic burst workloads.

Checklist: [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-2299), [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests with synthetic bursts, [x] perf benchmarks under 4 configs, [x] docs stub for Console (follow-up PR will add screenshots).

Design notes and tradeoffs: The rendezvous allocator uses a sliding similarity window keyed by (tenant_id, model_family, prompt_signature_hash). We intentionally keep the window conservative (default 250ms) to avoid combining unrelated requests; this reduces accidental over-merging. Prefill capacity is soft-reserved and reclaimed if downstream KV cache warms up within a grace period. Quant-consensus favors profiles with lower estimated loss above a configurable quality delta; if profiles are statistically indistinguishable, the system picks the lower-cost profile but enforces a minimum safety quant (e.g., 4-bit fallback disabled unless loss delta < 0.5%).

Review conversation (abridged):
- Liam O'Connor (review): "Nice approach — can we add a metric that shows effective tokens saved by rendezvous vs baseline? Also worried about tenant fairness when one tenant consistently preempts prefill slots."
  - Marina (reply): "Added unit_econ.tokens_saved counter and a per-tenant throttling knob (rendezvous.max_slots_per_tenant) with default 2; documented in code comments."
- Priya Natarajan (review): "Can quant_consensus be applied per-model-version or do we need to aggregate across versions? Concerned about fast rollouts seeding bad profiles."
  - Marina (reply): "Consensus is computed per model-major (family + major-version). We maintain a lightweight ledger of recent rollouts and a decay window to prevent aggressive flips; added tests for a 3-release scenario."
- Ethan Zhang (requested changes): "Perf harness flaky on GHA; move heavy runs to perf.yml and leave smoke in CI."
  - Marina (done): "Moved heavy runs to perf job, left smoke tests in PR CI. Updated workflow to upload perf artifacts to S3 for analysis."

CI and perf: The PR initially showed intermittent integration test failures caused by race conditions in the allocator reclaim path. I fixed it by switching a naive list traversal to an atomic compare-and-swap based reclaim loop and added a targeted unit test. The final CI run: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-smoke: pass, lint: pass, perf-benchmark: pass (job completed on perf runner; artifacts available).

Observability and rollout plan:
- Feature flag: feature.rendezvous_prefill_v1 (default off for all tenants).
- Canary: enabled for 5 pilot tenants with known bursty profiles for 48 hours.
- Monitoring: dashboards for rendezvous.group_size, prefill.hit_rate, quant.profile_switch_rate, and unit_econ.tokens_saved. Alert thresholds: prefill.hit_rate drop > 8% over baseline, profile_switch_rate > 10% in 1h.
- Fallback: automatic revert to safe-quant profile and disable rendezvous if unit-cost increases by > 20% in 1h.

Backward compatibility and cleanup: No public API changes. CLI flag is opt-in. Defaults are conservative; added a follow-up card (ENG-2310) to expose tenant-level tuning in Console and a small doc PR to show how to interpret cost-debug output.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals from all reviewers. Merge method: squash. Changelog entry prepared and tagged with release-candidate.

Notes for on-call and SRE: If you see increased false positives in alerts, first check telemetry.unit_econ.tokens_saved and rendezvous.group_size to determine if grouping is mis-specified for a tenant. The cost-debug CSV can be used to replay decisions offline and identify problematic signature collisions.

Related work and references: ENG-2299 design doc (link in Linear), a follow-up effort ENG-2310 for Console controls, and a downstream SDK change planned to expose --rendezvous-dryrun in the local dev container.
